statement: There exists an iid regenerative integer-time process Y_t that tends to +infinity almost surely, has deterministic regeneration displacement 1 and finite regeneration durations almost surely, but Y_t/t tends to 0 almost surely.
assumptions: iid positive integer durations T_i with P(T_i=m)=1/(m(m+1)), m>=1

source.author: w454
source.basis: Independent derivation before reading paired prover; contextual gap in Campos-Ramirez, Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 2.1, doi:10.1007/s00440-013-0527-7

proof: P(T>=m)=1/m, so T is finite a.s. and E[T]=infinity. For each M, the SLLN for min(T_i,M) gives liminf S_k/k>=E[min(T,M)]. Taking M to infinity gives S_k/k->infinity. Hence Y_t/t<=Y_t/S_{Y_t}->0 while Y_t->infinity.
remaining_gap: This regenerative holding process is not a uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor iid RWRE on Z^d. It refutes only the inference from finite-a.s. regeneration and bounded spatial increments to positive speed. No conclusion about C0041 itself.

statement: Let X start at 0 in Z^d and have nearest-neighbor transitions all at least kappa in (0,1). Let tau be an almost-surely finite nonnegative integer random time, R=max_{j<=tau}|X_j|_infinity, and D any event with P(D)=p>0. For every integer r,t>=0, P(tau>t|D)<=P(R>r|D)+p^-1 exp(-kappa^(2r+1) floor(t/(2r+1))). If P(R>r|D)<=C exp(-a r) for all r>=0 and a>2 log(1/kappa), then E[tau|D]<infinity.
assumptions: Fixed uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor Markov chain, or annealed mixture of such chains with common kappa
tau<infinity almost surely; tau need not be a stopping time
For the moment implication, exponential radius tail with stated strict rate threshold

proof: From any point in [-r,r]^d, 2r+1 successive +e_1 steps exit; their conditional probability is at least kappa^(2r+1). Iterate conditional survival bounds to bound the cube exit time. The event {tau>t,R<=r} is contained in survival to t. Conditioning is handled by division by p, not by assuming the conditioned chain retains ellipticity. Choose r=floor(c log(t+1)) with 1/a<c<1/(2 log(1/kappa)). The radius term is summable as t^-ac; the exit term is summable as exp(-c0 t^(1-2c log(1/kappa))/log(t+1)). Sum the tail.
remaining_gap: The needed exponential radius tail and its rate do not follow here from single-direction transience. Does not prove C0041.
